key_insight: The paper builds globally reliable and efficient computable error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinear PDEs, and shows they can be used directly as loss functions for neural approximations.
engineering_relevance: This enables physics-informed training with mathematically certified error control for parameterized nonlinear PDE solvers in engineering workflows.
method: Split the nonlinear operator into a linear residual plus a strongly monotone closure term.
Estimate the linear part with a discrete dual norm and replace the intractable closure norm by a computable surrogate satisfying pairing and Lipschitz bounds.
Prove two-sided global error bounds for first-order system least-squares and discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin formulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theorem-level results with explicit constants, verified assumptions for a model flux class, and applicability to arbitrary trial inputs, not just near the exact solution.
watch_item: The surrogate closure norm and all constants depend on the parameter range and must be implemented carefully to preserve the certified bounds.
paper_title: Global error estimators for parametric monotone nonlinearities and neural approximations
